question: Who along with Bhagat Singh, was the main accused in Assembly Bomb Case?A, Ram Prasad BismilB. AshafaqullaC. Surya SenD. Batukeshwar Dutta (RRB NTPC Tier I (27/04/2016) Shift 1)
options: C
B
D
A
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Batukeshwar Dutta

Explanation:
On April 8, 1929, Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutta threw a bomb in the Central Legislative Assembly in Delhi. The aim was to draw attention to revolutionary activities, and no one was killed. Both surrendered to the court to propagate their ideas. In this case, Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutta were the main accused. Ram Prasad Bismil and Ashfaqulla were associated with the Kakori Conspiracy, while Surya Sen led the Chittagong Armoury Raid. The Assembly Bomb Case brought fame to the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association.

question: Who among the following is known as the Father of Civil Services in India?A. Lord CornwallisB. Warren HastingsC. Lord WellesleyD. Lord William Bentinck (RRB NTPC Tier I (27/04/2016) Shift 3)
options: C
A
D
B
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Lord Cornwallis

Explanation:
Lord Cornwallis is known as the Father of Civil Services in India. He served as Governor-General of India from 1786 to 1793 and implemented several reforms to strengthen the administration. He prohibited civil servants from engaging in trade and private gain, laying the foundation for a professional and impartial bureaucracy. He also emphasized merit and hierarchy in appointments in coordination with the Court of Directors. During his tenure, the Permanent Settlement of Bengal was introduced. Thus, he is recognized as the founder of the Indian civil services.

☛ Under whose tenure was the Permanent Settlement introduced? → Lord Cornwallis
☛ What was Lord Cornwallis's tenure as Governor-General? → 1786-1793
☛ Who laid the foundation of modern bureaucracy in India? → Lord Cornwallis

question: The lady who played an important role in the awakening of Indian women to fight for independence and who is also known as Nightingale of India is –A. Vijaya Lakshmi PanditB. Durga Bai DeshmukhC. Sarojini NaiduD. Madam Bhikaiji Cama (RRB NTPC Tier I (27/04/2016) Shift 3)

question: Who among the following was one of the founders of the Swaraj Party?A. Motilal NehruB. Lala Lajpat RaiC. Subhas Chandra BoseD. Dadabhai Naoroji (RRB NTPC Tier I (28/04/2016) Shift 2)
options: A
C
B
D
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Motilal Nehru.

Explanation:
The Swaraj Party was founded on 1 January 1923. Its founders were Motilal Nehru and Chittaranjan Das. It emerged as a faction within the Indian National Congress, advocating a policy of non-cooperation with the British government by entering the legislative councils and obstructing the government from within. The party aimed to change the earlier policy of boycotting legislatures and instead enter them to disrupt the government. The Swaraj Party achieved success in the 1923 elections, becoming the largest party in the Central Legislative Assembly. Motilal Nehru later served as the President of the Indian National Congress.

question: . In order to help in the freedom struggle, which newspaper was started by Lokmanya Tilak?A. KesariB. Amrit Bazar PatrikaC. GhadarD. Harijan (RRB NTPC Tier I (28/04/2016) Shift 2)
options: B
A
C
D
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Kesari

Explanation:
Lokmanya Tilak started two newspapers in 1881: Kesari (Marathi) and Maratha (English). Through Kesari, he spread public awareness for the freedom struggle. It became a key platform for promoting Indian nationalism and criticizing British rule. Tilak was charged with sedition for articles in Kesari and was exiled to Mandalay jail. Kesari is still published today and symbolizes Tilak's legacy. question: Which movement was called off following the violence at 'Chauri Chaura' incident?A. Khilafat MovementB. Quit India MovementC. Non co-operation MovementD. Home Rule Movement (RRB NTPC Tier I (30/03/2016) Shift 3)

Explanation:
In 1922, at Chauri Chaura (Gorakhpur, Uttar Pradesh), protesters set fire to a police station, killing 22 policemen. Disturbed by this violence, Mahatma Gandhi called off the Non-co-operation Movement on 12 February 1922, as it violated the principle of non-violent Satyagraha. This movement had started in 1920, aiming at peaceful resistance against British rule. The Chauri Chaura incident challenged the ethos of non-violence, prompting Gandhi to halt the movement. Later, leaders like Chittaranjan Das and Motilal Nehru criticized this decision, leading to the formation of the Swaraj Party.

question: Which of the following was stated in the 'Gandhi-Irwin Pact' signed in March 1931? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (10/01/2021) Shift 2)
options: All Indians would get good education.
The manufacture of salt along the coast would be stopped.
Prisoners would not be released.
The Civil Disobedience Movement would be called off.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The Civil Disobedience Movement would be called off.

Explanation:
The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed on March 5, 1931, between Mahatma Gandhi and Viceroy Lord Irwin. Under this pact, the Congress agreed to call off the Civil Disobedience Movement and participate in the Second Round Table Conference. The government promised to release political prisoners, relax the salt laws, and withdraw all ordinances. However, the pact was not fully satisfactory, and later the Congress continued its demand for complete independence. This pact showed that the British government was compelled to acknowledge the pressure of the Indian national movement. It was a significant step in the Indian freedom struggle as it marked a temporary truce between the British and the Congress.

question: ___________ was celebrated as the First War of Indian Independence. (RRB NTPC CBT-I (10/01/2021) Shift 2)
options: The Uprising of 1857
The Rowlatt Satyagraha of 1919
The Santhal Revolt of 1855-56
The Civil War of 1861
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The Uprising of 1857

Explanation:
The Uprising of 1857, also known as the Indian Rebellion of 1857, was a major but ultimately unsuccessful uprising against the rule of the British East India Company. It began on 10 May 1857 in Meerut and soon spread to major parts of North India. The immediate cause was the introduction of the Enfield rifle with cartridges greased with animal fat, which offended both Hindu and Muslim soldiers. Deeper causes included political, social, economic, and religious grievances against British policies. Key leaders included Bahadur Shah Zafar, Rani Lakshmibai, Nana Saheb, Tatya Tope, and Mangal Pandey. Though the revolt failed, it marked the end of Company rule and the beginning of direct British Crown rule. It is considered the first collective attempt to achieve Indian independence.

question: Which of the following was a result of the Non-Cooperation and Khilafat movements? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (10/01/2021) Shift 2)

The working class went on strike in many towns and cities.

solution:

Explanation:
During the Non-Cooperation and Khilafat movements (1920-22), the working class participated in large-scale strikes, especially in cities like Bombay, Madras, and Calcutta. These movements were led by Mahatma Gandhi, who advocated non-violent non-cooperation. Workers showed their support through strikes and boycotts of British goods. In contrast, lawyers boycotted courts, students did not attend government-run institutions, and peasants refused to work for colonial officials. Thus, the working class strike was a significant result of these movements.

question: The Subsidiary Alliance was a non-intervention policy devised by _______ in 1798. (RRB NTPC CBT-I (11/01/2021) Shift 1)

Lord Wellesley
Lord Cornwallis
Lord Irwin
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Lord Wellesley

Explanation:
The Subsidiary Alliance system was devised by Lord Wellesley in 1798. It was a non-intervention policy that placed Indian states under British protection. Under this system, the Indian ruler had to disband his own army and accept British troops for his state's protection. The state had to pay for the maintenance of the British troops or cede territory. Lord Wellesley (1798-1805) was the Governor-General of British India and through this policy he expanded British influence across India. Several states such as Hyderabad, Awadh, Tanjore, etc. came under British control through this alliance. This policy helped the British to establish indirect control over Indian states without direct annexation.

चंद्रन देवनेसन ने 'द मेकिंग ऑफ द महात्मा' नामक पुस्तक लिखी थी, जिसमें दक्षिण अफ्रीका में महात्मा गांधी के जीवन और संघर्षों का विस्तार से वर्णन है। इस पुस्तक में उन्होंने कहा कि दक्षिण अफ्रीका ने गांधी को एक महान नेता और समाज सुधारक के रूप में ढाला। गांधी जी 1893 में दक्षिण अफ्रीका गए थे और वहां उन्होंने नस्लीय भेदभाव और अन्याय के खिलाफ सत्याग्रह और अहिंसक आंदोलन की नींव रखी। दक्षिण अफ्रीका में उनके अनुभवों ने उनके राजनीतिक और सामाजिक विचारों को गहराई से प्रभावित किया, जिसने बाद में भारत के स्वतंत्रता संग्राम में मार्गदर्शन किया।
